"""workflow-svc configuration.

The shared envelope (bind addresses, Postgres, NATS, OIDC, OTLP, audit HMAC
keys) comes from ``omnicore_svc_runtime.config.load_base("WORKFLOW")``, which
also derives:

- ``service_name`` -> ``"workflow-svc"``
- ``oidc_allowed_azp`` -> ``("workflow-bff", "shell-bff", "workflow-svc-worker")``
  unless ``WORKFLOW_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` overrides it.

workflow-svc adds its own execution-engine + AI model-lock fields on top:

- ``litellm_url`` / ``workflow_model_primary`` / ``workflow_model_fallback`` /
  ``workflow_model_temperature`` — forward-config for the AI Action / AI Agent
  node adapters (not yet consumed by this boot skeleton).
- ``exec_node_concurrency`` — per-layer node fan-out bound (ExecutionConsumer).
- ``http_allow_private`` — SSRF guard: allow private/RFC1918 egress from the
  ``http_request`` node (default off).
- ``dialogue_svc_addr`` / ``worker_client_id`` / ``worker_client_secret`` —
  the Broadcast node's outbound hop to dialogue-svc (#1394). See
  ``workflow_svc.dialogue`` for the auth posture these three feed.
- ``files_svc_addr`` / ``files_minio_bucket`` / ``qdrant_url`` /
  ``files_embedding_model`` — the Files & Data family's hops (#1407). See
  ``workflow_svc.files`` for the auth posture and for why one of those four is
  an object store and another is a vector database rather than all four being
  one gRPC address.
- ``ask_svc_addr`` / ``ask_svc_client_id`` / ``ask_svc_client_secret`` — the
  Ask node family's outbound leg (#1385). See
  ``workflow_svc.grpc_clients.ask_svc_client`` for why the worker mints its
  own token rather than forwarding the run initiator's.

One workflow-svc env var deliberately does NOT live here:
``WORKFLOW_DEEP_RESEARCH_ENABLED`` (#1366, the Research Assistant's gated
Deep tier) is read through
:func:`workflow_svc.nodes.content.deep_research_enabled` instead. It is
consumed by the node CATALOG and by a worker EXECUTOR — two processes, only
one of which builds a :class:`Config` — so routing it through this dataclass
would have meant either a second source of truth or threading a config object
down into `executors.py`, which every executor is deliberately free of. See
that function's docstring for why the read is live rather than captured.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from typing import Final

from omnicore_svc_runtime.config import (
    BaseServiceConfig,
    ConfigError,
    bool_env,
    int_env,
    load_base,
    optional_env,
)

# ConfigError is re-exported so callers (main.py, worker.py) catch it off this
# module rather than reaching into the runtime for the one exception this
# module's own load() can raise.
__all__ = ["ENV_PREFIX", "GOOSE_TABLE", "SCHEMA", "Config", "ConfigError", "load"]

ENV_PREFIX: Final = "WORKFLOW"
SCHEMA: Final = "workflow"
GOOSE_TABLE: Final = "goose_db_version_workflow"

# WORKFLOW tool dispatch (future stories) uses prompt-for-JSON against the LiteLLM
# gateway — native tool-calling 400s there. Model lock per the de-risk spike:
# PRIMARY qwen3.5:9b, FALLBACK gpt-oss:120b, temperature 0. Encoded here as
# documented defaults so later stories wire the dispatcher against them.
# TODO(workflow-runtime story): consume these in the AI Action / AI Agent node
# adapters; do NOT build the dispatcher in this boot-skeleton story.
_DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_PRIMARY: Final = "qwen3.5:9b"
_DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_FALLBACK: Final = "gpt-oss:120b"
_DEFAULT_EXEC_NODE_CONCURRENCY: Final = 5

# files-svc's OWN `FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL` default, deliberately — NOT one of
# the workflow model pins above. Document Query embeds its query and compares
# the vector against chunks files-svc embedded; two different models mean two
# different vector spaces and retrieval that returns confident noise. range-svc
# carries the identical `RANGE_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL` for the identical reason.
_DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL: Final = "nomic-embed-text:latest"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Config(BaseServiceConfig):
    """Immutable workflow-svc configuration. Construct via :func:`load`."""

    # AI / LiteLLM model lock (forward-config only — see module docstring TODO)
    litellm_url: str = "http://litellm:4000"
    workflow_model_primary: str = _DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_PRIMARY
    workflow_model_fallback: str = _DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_FALLBACK
    workflow_model_temperature: float = 0.0

    # Execution engine (P3 Task 6 — ExecutionConsumer)
    exec_node_concurrency: int = _DEFAULT_EXEC_NODE_CONCURRENCY
    http_allow_private: bool = False

    # Dialogue Nodes epic (#1394) — the Broadcast node's outbound hop from
    # workflow-svc-worker to dialogue-svc. ALL THREE must be set for the node
    # to run; any one blank leaves the client disabled by design (no network
    # attempt) and fails that ONE node with a user-safe reason rather than
    # crashing the worker.
    #
    # The two `worker_client_*` values are the worker's ONE service account,
    # not Dialogue's: the Media family's studio-svc hop (#1378) authenticates
    # with the same credential. It reads the same env vars directly rather
    # than through here because an executor is a module-level function with no
    # injection point (see `_build_studio_tts_client`), whereas this hop is
    # constructed in `worker.py`, which does have one.
    dialogue_svc_addr: str = ""
    worker_client_id: str = ""
    worker_client_secret: str = ""
    # Ask node family (#1385). Naming and shape mirror clio-svc's
    # agents-svc client (`AGENTS_SVC_ADDR`/`_CLIENT_ID`/`_CLIENT_SECRET`) —
    # the only other east-west Python client in the fleet. Addr AND secret
    # must both be set for the Ask-backed nodes (Deploy Survey / Load from
    # Ask / Ask Question); either missing disables the client and those nodes
    # then fail naming the absent config rather than a transport error. The
    # self-contained Ask nodes (Generate Survey, Test Survey) never read
    # these. The token URL is DERIVED from the OIDC envelope rather than
    # configured separately, so it cannot drift from the issuer this service
    # already verifies against.
    ask_svc_addr: str = ""
    ask_svc_client_id: str = "workflow-svc-worker"
    ask_svc_client_secret: str = ""

    # Files & Data node family (#1407). Read here for the worker's boot log
    # only: the executors themselves read these same env vars directly through
    # `filesdata_executors._build_*`, because an executor is a module-level
    # function with no injection point (the same reason
    # `_build_studio_tts_client` does). Having them on Config is what lets
    # `worker.py` say at startup which of the five nodes will actually work,
    # rather than each node discovering it the first time a run reaches it.
    #
    # `files_minio_bucket` (FILES_BUCKET_NAME — files-svc's own env name, so
    # a compose file cannot point the two halves of this hop at different
    # buckets) + the MINIO_* values are needed because
    # `DocumentService.Upload` takes a bucket-relative object key and never
    # bytes — files-svc "does not handle bytes" by design, so a caller that
    # wants to save content must put the object itself first, exactly as
    # files-bff's Upload handler does.
    #
    # `qdrant_url` + `files_embedding_model` back Document Query, which reads
    # the `files_chunks_{org_id}` collection files-svc writes rather than a
    # files-svc RPC (there is none). The model MUST match the one files-svc
    # embedded those chunks with or retrieval returns noise — see
    # `workflow_svc.files.search`.
    files_svc_addr: str = ""
    files_minio_bucket: str = ""
    qdrant_url: str = ""
    files_embedding_model: str = _DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL


def load() -> Config:
    """Load Config from process env. Raises ConfigError on missing required vars."""
    base = load_base(ENV_PREFIX)
    return Config(
        **{f.name: getattr(base, f.name) for f in fields(base)},
        litellm_url=optional_env("LITELLM_URL", "http://litellm:4000"),
        workflow_model_primary=optional_env(
            "WORKFLOW_MODEL_PRIMARY", _DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_PRIMARY
        ),
        workflow_model_fallback=optional_env(
            "WORKFLOW_MODEL_FALLBACK", _DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODEL_FALLBACK
        ),
        workflow_model_temperature=0.0,
        exec_node_concurrency=int_env(
            "WORKFLOW_EXEC_NODE_CONCURRENCY", _DEFAULT_EXEC_NODE_CONCURRENCY
        ),
        http_allow_private=bool_env("WORKFLOW_HTTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE"),
        dialogue_svc_addr=optional_env("DIALOGUE_SVC_ADDR", ""),
        worker_client_id=optional_env("WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_ID", "workflow-svc-worker"),
        worker_client_secret=optional_env("WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET", ""),
        files_svc_addr=optional_env("FILES_SVC_ADDR", ""),
        files_minio_bucket=optional_env("FILES_BUCKET_NAME", ""),
        qdrant_url=optional_env("QDRANT_URL", ""),
        files_embedding_model=optional_env(
            "WORKFLOW_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL", _DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL
        ),
        ask_svc_addr=optional_env("ASK_SVC_ADDR"),
        ask_svc_client_id=optional_env("ASK_SVC_CLIENT_ID", "workflow-svc-worker"),
        ask_svc_client_secret=optional_env("ASK_SVC_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    )

"""workflow-svc orchestrator + graceful shutdown (#1310 boot skeleton).

Wiring sequence (mirrors services/clio-svc/src/clio_svc/main.py and
services/range-svc/src/range_svc/main.py):

    load config
      -> bootstrap observability (logger + tracer + meter)
      -> setup OIDC JWT verifier (aud + azp allowlist — Gate 2)
      -> connect NATS
      -> build gRPC server (mTLS interceptor + health + reflection)
      -> register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers
      -> serve until signal
      -> graceful shutdown (stop server, close NATS, shutdown meter + tracer)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import signal
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from omnicore_svc_runtime.db import migrate as db_migrate
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate import RoleCredential
from omnicore_svc_runtime.observability.request_metrics import set_service_up

from workflow_svc import config as cfg_mod
from workflow_svc.audit import parse_keys
from workflow_svc.auth import create_verifier
from workflow_svc.db import Pool, create_pool
from workflow_svc.events import Outbox
from workflow_svc.events import connect as nats_connect
from workflow_svc.grpc_clients import build_ask_client
from workflow_svc.observability import (
    configure_logger,
    get_logger,
    setup_meter,
    setup_tracer,
    shutdown_meter,
    shutdown_tracer,
)
from workflow_svc.server import build_server


def _migrations_dir() -> Path:
    """Locate the migrations dir relative to the package install root.

    In the container: ``/app/migrations`` (Dockerfile COPY target).
    Outside (dev / tests): two levels up from this file
    (``src/workflow_svc/main.py`` -> ``services/workflow-svc/migrations``).
    Mirrors range-svc.
    """
    container = Path("/app/migrations")
    if container.exists():
        return container
    here = Path(__file__).resolve()
    return here.parent.parent.parent / "migrations"


async def _serve(c: cfg_mod.Config) -> int:
    """Bring up every long-lived dependency and serve until SIGINT/SIGTERM."""
    log = get_logger("main")

    setup_tracer(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("tracer ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    setup_meter(
        service_name=c.service_name,
        otlp_endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=c.otlp_insecure,
    )
    log.info("meter ready", endpoint=c.otlp_endpoint, insecure=c.otlp_insecure)

    verifier = await create_verifier(
        issuer_url=c.oidc_issuer_url,
        internal_url=c.oidc_internal_url,
        audience=c.oidc_audience,
        allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp,
    )
    log.info("oidc verifier ready", audience=c.oidc_audience, allowed_azp=c.oidc_allowed_azp)

    publisher = await nats_connect(
        nats_url=c.nats_url, creds_file=c.nats_creds_file, ca_file=c.nats_ca_file
    )
    log.info("nats connected", url=c.nats_url)

    # Startup migrations (goose) + per-role LOGIN provisioning, BEFORE the app
    # pool opens — workflow_app / workflow_migrate / workflow_drainer are
    # created NOLOGIN by migration 00001, so the pool can only authenticate
    # once `up` has rotated their passwords. Empty admin DSN → skipped
    # (mirrors range-svc / clio-svc).
    await db_migrate.up(
        admin_dsn=c.postgres_admin_dsn,
        migrations_dir=_migrations_dir(),
        goose_table=cfg_mod.GOOSE_TABLE,
        service="workflow-svc",
        roles=(
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_app", password=c.app_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_migrate", password=c.migrate_db_password),
            RoleCredential(role=f"{cfg_mod.SCHEMA}_drainer", password=c.drainer_db_password),
        ),
    )
    log.info("startup migrations complete")

    pool: Pool = await create_pool(
        dsn=c.postgres_dsn,
        migrator_dsn=c.postgres_migrator_dsn,
        drainer_dsn=c.postgres_drainer_dsn,
        max_size=c.postgres_max_conns,
        min_size=c.postgres_min_conns,
        max_inactive_connection_lifetime=c.postgres_max_conn_idle_time_s,
    )
    log.info(
        "postgres pool ready",
        migrator=pool.migrator is not None,
        drainer=pool.drainer is not None,
    )

    # Transactional outbox drainer. Runs in the server process, mirroring
    # range-svc / clio-svc: domain handlers write workflow.event_outbox rows
    # in their own tx; this background loop forwards them to NATS with
    # Nats-Msg-Id dedup. workflow-svc-worker runs its own two ExecutionConsumer
    # instances (run + resume) in a separate process — this drainer is a
    # publisher, not a consumer, and lives here regardless.
    background: list[asyncio.Task[None]] = []
    outbox = Outbox(pool=pool, publisher=publisher, schema=cfg_mod.SCHEMA)
    background.append(asyncio.create_task(outbox.run(), name="outbox"))

    audit_keys = parse_keys(c.audit_hmac_keys, active_id=c.audit_hmac_active_key_id)

    ask_client = build_ask_client(c)
    if ask_client.enabled:
        log.info("ask client enabled", addr=c.ask_svc_addr)

    set_service_up(version=c.service_name)
    server = build_server(
        verifier=verifier,
        grpc_addr=c.grpc_addr,
        mtls_cert_file=c.mtls_cert_file,
        mtls_key_file=c.mtls_key_file,
        mtls_ca_file=c.mtls_ca_file,
        healthz_addr=c.healthz_addr,
        metrics_addr=c.metrics_addr,
        pool=pool,
        audit_keys=audit_keys,
        http_allow_private=c.http_allow_private,
        # "Test this node" (ExecutionService.RunNode) dispatches the same
        # executors the async engine does, in THIS process, so the Ask family
        # needs its client here as well as in workflow-svc-worker (#1385).
        # `build_ask_client` returns a disabled client when the config is
        # absent, so a deployment with no Ask wiring boots unchanged.
        ask_client=ask_client,
    )
    await server.grpc_server.start()
    log.info("server listening", grpc=c.grpc_addr, healthz=c.healthz_addr, metrics=c.metrics_addr)

    stop_event = asyncio.Event()
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    def _signal_handler() -> None:
        log.info("shutdown signal received")
        stop_event.set()

    for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
        loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _signal_handler)

    try:
        await stop_event.wait()
    finally:
        log.info("graceful shutdown begin")
        for t in background:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*background, return_exceptions=True)
        await server.stop(grace_s=10.0)
        await ask_client.close()
        await publisher.close()
        await pool.close()
        shutdown_meter()
        shutdown_tracer()
        log.info("graceful shutdown complete")

    return 0


def main() -> int:
    """Process entrypoint. Returns the desired exit code."""
    configure_logger(level="INFO")
    log = get_logger("main")
    try:
        c = cfg_mod.load()
    except cfg_mod.ConfigError as exc:
        log.error("config load failed", err=str(exc))
        return 1
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_serve(c))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

  1. ``platform/keycloak/realm-export.json`` — the ``workflow-svc-worker``

     membership test, so each target's JWTVerifier accepts the call while the
     worker's own workflow-svc calls keep working.
  2. That target's ``*_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` (``platform/compose/<svc>.yml``)

client_credentials token carries no ``org_id``, so the ``tenant:any`` realm
grant is what lets it adopt ``x-tenant-id``. See
:mod:`workflow_svc.dialogue` for that.

sidecar reconciles ``realm-export.json`` against live Keycloak on every stack
start with ``IMPORT_CACHE_ENABLED=false``.

Still required for either path to actually run: the workflow-svc-worker
process needs that hop's ``*_SVC_ADDR`` and
``WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET`` in its environment. Without them the
client stays disabled by design (no network attempt) and the affected node
fails that ONE node with a user-safe reason rather than crashing the worker.

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import httpx

# Refresh this many seconds before the cached token's actual expiry, so a call
# that starts just before expiry never races a token that dies mid-RPC.
_REFRESH_SKEW_S = 30.0

_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=10.0, write=5.0, pool=5.0)


class ServiceAccountTokenError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the token endpoint returns a non-2xx response.

    The exception message NEVER includes the client secret — the secret is sent
    only in the request body, never interpolated into a log line or an
    exception message.
    """


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ServiceAccountTokenSource:
    """Mints + caches an OIDC ``client_credentials`` access token.

    ``client_secret`` is sent ONLY in the POST body of the token request — it is
    never logged, never included in an exception message, and never echoed back
    in any return value.
    """

    token_url: str
    client_id: str
    client_secret: str
    http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None
    _owns_client: bool = field(init=False, default=False)
    _cached_token: str = field(init=False, default="")
    _expires_at_monotonic: float = field(init=False, default=0.0)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.http_client is None:
            self.http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
            self._owns_client = True

    async def get_token(self) -> str:
        """Return a cached, still-valid access token, minting a fresh one when
        the cache is empty or within ``_REFRESH_SKEW_S`` of expiry."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        if self._cached_token and now < self._expires_at_monotonic:
            return self._cached_token

        assert self.http_client is not None  # set in __post_init__
        resp = await self.http_client.post(
            self.token_url,
            data={
                "grant_type": "client_credentials",
                "client_id": self.client_id,
                "client_secret": self.client_secret,
            },
        )
        if not resp.is_success:
            # Never interpolate resp.text — Keycloak error bodies do not echo
            # the secret, but treat the endpoint's response as opaque on
            # principle.
            raise ServiceAccountTokenError(f"token endpoint returned {resp.status_code}")
        body = resp.json()
        # A malformed-but-200 response must not escape as a bare KeyError:
        # every caller catches ServiceAccountTokenError and turns it into a
        # node failure_reason, so an unwrapped KeyError would crash the node
        # with something no operator can act on. Caching `str(None)` would be
        # worse still — the client would then send `Bearer None` on every
        # call until the process restarted. Carried over from the Ask hop's
        # own token source (#1385) when that second copy was folded in here.
        raw = body.get("access_token")
        if not raw:
            raise ServiceAccountTokenError("token endpoint returned no access_token")
        token = str(raw)
        expires_in = float(body.get("expires_in", 300))
        self._cached_token = token
        self._expires_at_monotonic = now + max(expires_in - _REFRESH_SKEW_S, 0.0)
        return token

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self._owns_client and self.http_client is not None:
            await self.http_client.aclose()

            _log.debug("signal handler unavailable on this platform", signal=sig)

    # Read once here rather than per message. An unset key is tolerated at
    # boot — it only matters to a canvas that actually uses the node, and
    # crashlooping the worker (and with it every OTHER consumer this process
    # runs) over an unused feature's secret is the wrong trade. `mint` raises
    # and `verify` returns False on an empty key, so the failure is loud and
    # fail-closed at the point it matters.
    tenant_assertion_key = load_tenant_assertion_key() or b""
    if not tenant_assertion_key:
        _log.warning(
            "no tenant-assertion key resolved (Vault, then NATS_TENANT_ASSERTION_KEY) "
            "— queue results will be REJECTED and add_to_queue nodes will stay parked; "
            "every other node type is unaffected"
        )
    # Dialogue Nodes epic (#1394). Disabled — no channel, no token, no network
    # attempt — unless BOTH DIALOGUE_SVC_ADDR and
    # WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET are set. Disabled is a supported state:
    # a Broadcast node then fails that ONE node with a clear reason instead of
    # the worker refusing to start, so an operator who has not wired Dialogue
    # yet still gets every other node type. See workflow_svc.dialogue's package
    # docstring for the Keycloak mappers and azp allowlist this depends on.
    dialogue_token_source = (
        ServiceAccountTokenSource(
            token_url=(
                f"{(cfg.oidc_internal_url or cfg.oidc_issuer_url).rstrip('/')}"
                "/protocol/openid-connect/token"
            ),
            client_id=cfg.worker_client_id,
            client_secret=cfg.worker_client_secret,
        )
        if cfg.worker_client_secret
        else None
    )
    dialogue_client = DialogueClient(addr=cfg.dialogue_svc_addr, token_source=dialogue_token_source)
    _log.info("dialogue client", enabled=dialogue_client.enabled, addr=cfg.dialogue_svc_addr)

    # Files & Data node family (#1407). Logged, NOT constructed here: the five
    # executors build their own clients through
    # `filesdata_executors._build_*`, the module-level seam the Media family's
    # studio-svc hop already uses (an executor is a module-level function with
    # no injection point). This line exists so an operator learns at BOOT which
    # of the five nodes can work, instead of each one discovering it the first
    # time a run reaches it — and so a half-wired deployment (files-svc but no
    # MinIO, say) is visible before it produces a puzzling per-node failure.
    _log.info(
        "files integration",
        # A read node needs files-svc plus the worker's service-account
        # credential; without either, every one of the five fails.
        reads_enabled=bool(cfg.files_svc_addr and cfg.worker_client_secret),
        # Saving additionally needs somewhere to put the bytes, because
        # DocumentService.Upload takes a key and not content.
        writes_enabled=bool(
            cfg.files_svc_addr and cfg.worker_client_secret and cfg.files_minio_bucket
        ),

        # embeddings gateway; the other four do not touch either.

    # gRPC channel is multiplexed and the token source caches, so a second
    # client would only double the token grants.

    # class: the resume envelope carries the run-job payload shape, so the
    # handler needs no branch — it re-enters the ledger-seeded walk, which is

        # same nodes, and two clients would mean two gRPC channels and two

    )

    # succeeded execution out to its downstream chain triggers. Same
    # BYPASSRLS drainer path, no NATS subscription of its own.
    chain_trigger = ChainTriggerWorker(pool=pool, audit_keys=audit_keys)
    chain_trigger_task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.create_task(
        chain_trigger.run(), name="chain-trigger"
    )

    # than either workflow stream: the message is queue-svc's event, published
    # by queue-svc's own outbox, and a vertical does not publish onto another
    # vertical's work-queue stream.

        publisher=publisher,
        pool=pool,
        assertion_key=tenant_assertion_key,
    )
    queue_result_task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.create_task(
        queue_result_consumer.run(), name="queue-result-consumer"
    )
    _log.info("queue result consumer started", durable=QueuePostResultConsumer.durable_name)

    # JetStream stream, and the two subjects this feature needs only reach
    # EVENTS when a rebuilt ws-gateway or notifications-svc calls
    # eventbus.EnsureStream. Rebuilding just the workflow/queue verticals
    # therefore leaves the publisher talking to a stream that does not claim
    # its subject — the node parks forever with nothing in the UI to say why.
    # Read-only: it reports, it does not provision. See stream_check's module
    # docstring for why a second provisioning owner would be worse.
    await warn_on_unclaimed_subjects(publisher.js)

    # a timer — because the failure it covers is the ABSENCE of a message, and
    # nothing else in this process would ever notice.
    queue_park_reaper = QueueParkReaper(pool=pool)
    reaper_task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.create_task(
        queue_park_reaper.run(), name="queue-park-reaper"
    )

        _request_shutdown()

    stop_task = asyncio.create_task(_stop_event.wait(), name="stop-waiter")
    try:
        done, _pending = await asyncio.wait(
            {
                stop_task,
                consumer_task,
                resume_task,
                trigger_scheduler_task,
                chain_trigger_task,
                queue_result_task,
                reaper_task,
            },
            return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
        )
        for task in done:
            if task is not stop_task and not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is not None:
                # A dead consumer (e.g. ConsumerConfigMismatchError on a stale
                # durable) is FATAL: exit nonzero so an on-failure restart
                # policy restarts the worker and dashboards surface the
                # failure — a clean exit 0 here would mean no restart and a
                # green status for a worker that consumes nothing (triage #14).
                # ANY of the three dying is fatal — a live run-job consumer
                # with a dead resume or queue-result consumer would accept work
                # and then never wake anything it parked.
                _log.error("consumer exited", task=task.get_name(), err=str(task.exception()))
                exit_code = 1
    finally:
        _log.info("workflow-svc-worker shutdown begin")
        await consumer.close()
        await resume_consumer.close()
        await trigger_scheduler.close()
        await chain_trigger.close()
        await queue_result_consumer.close()
        await queue_park_reaper.close()
        # Closed once, not once per consumer — both share the instance.
        await dialogue_client.close()
        consumer_task.cancel()
        resume_task.cancel()
        trigger_scheduler_task.cancel()
        chain_trigger_task.cancel()
        queue_result_task.cancel()
        reaper_task.cancel()
        if not stop_task.done():
            stop_task.cancel()
        # Every task this worker started, or shutdown silently leaves one
        # running.
        await asyncio.gather(
            consumer_task,
            resume_task,
            trigger_scheduler_task,
            chain_trigger_task,
            queue_result_task,
            reaper_task,
            stop_task,
            return_exceptions=True,
        )
        await ask_client.close()
        await publisher.close()
        await pool.close()
        shutdown_meter()
        healthz_server.shutdown()
        healthz_server.server_close()
        _log.info("workflow-svc-worker shutdown complete")

    return exit_code


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Process entrypoint. Returns the desired exit code."""
    configure_logger(level="INFO")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="workflow_svc.worker",
        description="workflow-svc-worker: JetStream consumer host (ExecutionConsumer)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--once",
        action="store_true",
        help="run one idle cycle and exit (integration-test mode)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = cfg_mod.load()
    except cfg_mod.ConfigError as exc:
        structlog.stdlib.get_logger("workflow_svc.worker").error("config load failed", err=str(exc))
        return 1
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_serve(cfg, once=args.once))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

- ``files_svc_addr`` / ``files_minio_bucket`` / ``qdrant_url`` /
  ``files_embedding_model`` — the Files & Data family's hops (#1407). See

class _MetricsHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Prometheus scrape endpoint on GET /metrics."""

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        from prometheus_client import CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST, generate_latest

        if self.path == "/metrics":
            body = generate_latest()
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)
        else:
            self.send_response(404)
            self.end_headers()

    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: object) -> None:
        pass  # silence access logs in tests


def _build_metrics(addr: str) -> tuple[HTTPServer, asyncio.Task[None]]:
    """Run a tiny HTTP /metrics server on ``addr`` (e.g. ":9100") in a thread-bound task."""
    host, _, port_str = addr.rpartition(":")
    host = host or "0.0.0.0"  # noqa: S104
    srv = HTTPServer((host, int(port_str)), _MetricsHandler)
    task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
        asyncio.to_thread(srv.serve_forever)

"""ServiceAccountTokenSource — OIDC ``client_credentials`` token minting.

Shared by every outbound cross-vertical hop workflow-svc-worker makes: the
Media family's studio-svc calls (#1378, :mod:`workflow_svc.studio.tts_client`)
and the Broadcast node's dialogue-svc calls (#1394,
:mod:`workflow_svc.dialogue.client`). Both need a bearer JWT because the
target service requires one on EVERY RPC, and a workflow run is executed long
after the requesting user's token is gone.

**This is a deliberate FORK of studio-svc's ``studio_svc/files/token.py``**,
which does the identical job for the studio-svc -> files-svc hop. It is copied
rather than promoted into ``omnicore_svc_runtime`` for one reason: anything
under ``platform/libs/python/**`` pulls every Python service into CI scope and
has to clear ``check-shared-lib-sync`` for all ten consumers, which is a far
larger blast radius than either issue warrants. The repo already carries this
shape of fork knowingly (see the eight forked runtime auth interceptors).
Consolidating all of them into the shared runtime is worth doing on its own,
separately.

What that argument does NOT justify is a second copy inside workflow-svc, so
this module is the single home for both hops rather than one per vertical
package.

GATE 2 WIRING, per target service (both halves required; either alone fails
closed):

  1. ``platform/keycloak/realm-export.json`` — the ``workflow-svc-worker``
     client carries one audience mapper PER target, so its
     client_credentials token is minted with
     ``aud=[workflow-svc, studio-svc, dialogue-svc]``,
     ``azp=workflow-svc-worker``. pyjwt treats a multi-valued ``aud`` as a
     membership test, so each target's JWTVerifier accepts the call while the
     worker's own workflow-svc calls keep working.
  2. That target's ``*_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` (``platform/compose/<svc>.yml``)
     includes ``workflow-svc-worker`` — see ``STUDIO_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` and
     ``DIALOGUE_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP``.

dialogue-svc adds a THIRD gate the studio hop does not need: a
client_credentials token carries no ``org_id``, so the ``tenant:any`` realm
grant is what lets it adopt ``x-tenant-id``. See
:mod:`workflow_svc.dialogue` for that.

The realm change needs no manual re-import: the ``keycloak-config-cli``
sidecar reconciles ``realm-export.json`` against live Keycloak on every stack
start with ``IMPORT_CACHE_ENABLED=false``.

Still required for either path to actually run: the workflow-svc-worker
process needs that hop's ``*_SVC_ADDR`` and
``WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET`` in its environment. Without them the
client stays disabled by design (no network attempt) and the affected node
fails that ONE node with a user-safe reason rather than crashing the worker.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import httpx

# Refresh this many seconds before the cached token's actual expiry, so a call
# that starts just before expiry never races a token that dies mid-RPC.
_REFRESH_SKEW_S = 30.0

_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=10.0, write=5.0, pool=5.0)


class ServiceAccountTokenError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the token endpoint returns a non-2xx response.

    The exception message NEVER includes the client secret — the secret is sent
    only in the request body, never interpolated into a log line or an
    exception message.
    """


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ServiceAccountTokenSource:
    """Mints + caches an OIDC ``client_credentials`` access token.

    ``client_secret`` is sent ONLY in the POST body of the token request — it is
    never logged, never included in an exception message, and never echoed back
    in any return value.
    """

    token_url: str
    client_id: str
    client_secret: str
    http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None
    _owns_client: bool = field(init=False, default=False)
    _cached_token: str = field(init=False, default="")
    _expires_at_monotonic: float = field(init=False, default=0.0)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.http_client is None:
            self.http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
            self._owns_client = True

    async def get_token(self) -> str:
        """Return a cached, still-valid access token, minting a fresh one when
        the cache is empty or within ``_REFRESH_SKEW_S`` of expiry."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        if self._cached_token and now < self._expires_at_monotonic:
            return self._cached_token

        assert self.http_client is not None  # set in __post_init__
        resp = await self.http_client.post(
            self.token_url,
            data={
                "grant_type": "client_credentials",
                "client_id": self.client_id,
                "client_secret": self.client_secret,
            },
        )
        if not resp.is_success:
            # Never interpolate resp.text — Keycloak error bodies do not echo
            # the secret, but treat the endpoint's response as opaque on
            # principle.
            raise ServiceAccountTokenError(f"token endpoint returned {resp.status_code}")
        body = resp.json()
        # A malformed-but-200 response must not escape as a bare KeyError:
        # every caller catches ServiceAccountTokenError and turns it into a
        # node failure_reason, so an unwrapped KeyError would crash the node
        # with something no operator can act on. Caching `str(None)` would be
        # worse still — the client would then send `Bearer None` on every
        # call until the process restarted. Carried over from the Ask hop's
        # own token source (#1385) when that second copy was folded in here.
        raw = body.get("access_token")
        if not raw:
            raise ServiceAccountTokenError("token endpoint returned no access_token")
        token = str(raw)
        expires_in = float(body.get("expires_in", 300))
        self._cached_token = token
        self._expires_at_monotonic = now + max(expires_in - _REFRESH_SKEW_S, 0.0)
        return token

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self._owns_client and self.http_client is not None:
            await self.http_client.aclose()

"""workflow-svc-worker entrypoint (Workflows P3, Task 6).

The worker is the second long-lived process built from the workflow-svc
container image — same package, same wiring code, but launched as
``python -m workflow_svc.worker`` instead of ``python -m workflow_svc``.

  - bootstraps observability (logger + meter)
  - binds the /healthz HTTPServer so the workflow-svc-worker compose layer is
    health-green
  - opens the Postgres pool (``workflow_app`` request path + optional drainer)
    and loads the audit-HMAC key set

    (``workflow.execution.run.>`` on the ``WORKFLOW_EXECUTE`` stream) — the DAG
    engine loop that executes workflow canvases as topological layers, plus its
    resume binding and the ``QueuePostResultConsumer`` that unparks an
    ``add_to_queue`` node when Queue answers (#1390)

to the single execution consumer this vertical needs.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import os
import signal
import sys

import structlog
from omnicore_svc_runtime.tenant_assertion import load_key as load_tenant_assertion_key

from workflow_svc import config as cfg_mod
from workflow_svc.audit import parse_keys
from workflow_svc.db import create_pool
from workflow_svc.dialogue import DialogueClient
from workflow_svc.events import connect as nats_connect
from workflow_svc.grpc_clients import build_ask_client
from workflow_svc.observability import configure_logger, setup_meter, shutdown_meter
from workflow_svc.serviceauth import ServiceAccountTokenSource
from workflow_svc.workers.execution.consumer import ExecutionConsumer
from workflow_svc.workers.healthz import start_healthz_server
from workflow_svc.workers.queue_result.consumer import QueuePostResultConsumer
from workflow_svc.workers.queue_result.reaper import QueueParkReaper
from workflow_svc.workers.queue_result.stream_check import warn_on_unclaimed_subjects
from workflow_svc.workers.triggers.chain import ChainTriggerWorker
from workflow_svc.workers.triggers.scheduler import TriggerSchedulerWorker

_log = structlog.stdlib.get_logger("workflow_svc.worker")

_DEFAULT_HEALTHZ_PORT = 8081


def _parse_healthz_port() -> int:
    """Extract port number from WORKFLOW_WORKER_HEALTHZ_ADDR (e.g. ':8081')."""
    addr = os.environ.get("WORKFLOW_WORKER_HEALTHZ_ADDR", f":{_DEFAULT_HEALTHZ_PORT}")
    try:
        return int(addr.lstrip(":"))
    except ValueError:
        return _DEFAULT_HEALTHZ_PORT


_stop_event: asyncio.Event | None = None


def _request_shutdown() -> None:
    """Idempotent shutdown signal — called from SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers."""
    if _stop_event is not None:
        _stop_event.set()


async def _serve(cfg: cfg_mod.Config, *, once: bool = False) -> int:
    """Bootstrap deps, run the execution + resume consumers until signal."""
    global _stop_event
    _stop_event = asyncio.Event()

    _log.info("workflow-svc-worker starting")

    setup_meter(
        service_name=f"{cfg.service_name}-worker",
        otlp_endpoint=cfg.otlp_endpoint,
        insecure=cfg.otlp_insecure,
    )

    # Postgres pool: every ledger/claim/finish write runs via the workflow_app
    # request path (pool.with_org GUC), NOT the SELECT-only drainer role.
    pool = await create_pool(
        dsn=cfg.postgres_dsn,
        migrator_dsn=cfg.postgres_migrator_dsn,
        drainer_dsn=cfg.postgres_drainer_dsn,
        max_size=cfg.postgres_max_conns,
        min_size=cfg.postgres_min_conns,
        max_inactive_connection_lifetime=cfg.postgres_max_conn_idle_time_s,
    )
    _log.info("postgres pool ready", drainer=pool.drainer is not None)

    audit_keys = parse_keys(cfg.audit_hmac_keys, active_id=cfg.audit_hmac_active_key_id)

    publisher = await nats_connect(
        nats_url=cfg.nats_url, creds_file=cfg.nats_creds_file, ca_file=cfg.nats_ca_file
    )
    _log.info("nats connected", url=cfg.nats_url)

    _log.info("healthz listening", port=port)

        try:
            loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _request_shutdown)
        except NotImplementedError:
            # add_signal_handler is unavailable on some platforms/event loops
            # (e.g. Windows, non-main-thread loops). Safe to ignore — shutdown
            # still works via the _stop_event path.
            _log.debug("signal handler unavailable on this platform", signal=sig)

    # P0-13 key for the cross-vertical Add to Queue request/reply (#1390).
    # Read once here rather than per message. An unset key is tolerated at
    # boot — it only matters to a canvas that actually uses the node, and
    # crashlooping the worker (and with it every OTHER consumer this process
    # runs) over an unused feature's secret is the wrong trade. `mint` raises
    # and `verify` returns False on an empty key, so the failure is loud and
    # fail-closed at the point it matters.
    tenant_assertion_key = load_tenant_assertion_key() or b""
    if not tenant_assertion_key:
        _log.warning(
            "no tenant-assertion key resolved (Vault, then NATS_TENANT_ASSERTION_KEY) "
            "— queue results will be REJECTED and add_to_queue nodes will stay parked; "
            "every other node type is unaffected"
        )
    # Dialogue Nodes epic (#1394). Disabled — no channel, no token, no network
    # attempt — unless BOTH DIALOGUE_SVC_ADDR and
    # WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET are set. Disabled is a supported state:
    # a Broadcast node then fails that ONE node with a clear reason instead of
    # the worker refusing to start, so an operator who has not wired Dialogue
    # yet still gets every other node type. See workflow_svc.dialogue's package
    # docstring for the Keycloak mappers and azp allowlist this depends on.
    dialogue_token_source = (
        ServiceAccountTokenSource(
            token_url=(
                f"{(cfg.oidc_internal_url or cfg.oidc_issuer_url).rstrip('/')}"
                "/protocol/openid-connect/token"
            ),
            client_id=cfg.worker_client_id,
            client_secret=cfg.worker_client_secret,
        )
        if cfg.worker_client_secret
        else None
    )
    dialogue_client = DialogueClient(addr=cfg.dialogue_svc_addr, token_source=dialogue_token_source)
    _log.info("dialogue client", enabled=dialogue_client.enabled, addr=cfg.dialogue_svc_addr)

    # Files & Data node family (#1407). Logged, NOT constructed here: the five
    # executors build their own clients through
    # `filesdata_executors._build_*`, the module-level seam the Media family's
    # studio-svc hop already uses (an executor is a module-level function with
    # no injection point). This line exists so an operator learns at BOOT which
    # of the five nodes can work, instead of each one discovering it the first
    # time a run reaches it — and so a half-wired deployment (files-svc but no
    # MinIO, say) is visible before it produces a puzzling per-node failure.
    _log.info(
        "files integration",
        # A read node needs files-svc plus the worker's service-account
        # credential; without either, every one of the five fails.
        reads_enabled=bool(cfg.files_svc_addr and cfg.worker_client_secret),
        # Saving additionally needs somewhere to put the bytes, because
        # DocumentService.Upload takes a key and not content.
        writes_enabled=bool(
            cfg.files_svc_addr and cfg.worker_client_secret and cfg.files_minio_bucket
        ),
        # Document Query additionally needs the vector store AND the
        # embeddings gateway; the other four do not touch either.
        search_enabled=bool(cfg.qdrant_url and cfg.litellm_url),
        addr=cfg.files_svc_addr,
        embedding_model=cfg.files_embedding_model,
    )

    # gRPC channel is multiplexed and the token source caches, so a second
    # client would only double the token grants.

        _log.info("ask-svc client enabled", addr=cfg.ask_svc_addr)
    else:

        publisher=publisher,
        pool=pool,
        audit_keys=audit_keys,
        node_concurrency=cfg.exec_node_concurrency,
        allow_private=cfg.http_allow_private,
        dialogue=dialogue_client,
        ask_client=ask_client,
    )

        consumer.run(), name="execution-consumer"
    )
    _log.info("execution consumer started", durable=ExecutionConsumer.DURABLE_NAME)

    # Parked-run resume consumer (#1402 PR B). A SECOND binding of the same
    # class: the resume envelope carries the run-job payload shape, so the
    # handler needs no branch — it re-enters the ledger-seeded walk, which is
    # what resume was already built to do. It must be a separate durable
    # because the subjects live on a different stream (WORKFLOW_SCHEDULE has
    # `limits` retention + ADR-51 flags, which WORKFLOW_EXECUTE cannot have).
    resume_consumer = ExecutionConsumer(
        publisher=publisher,
        pool=pool,
        audit_keys=audit_keys,
        node_concurrency=cfg.exec_node_concurrency,
        allow_private=cfg.http_allow_private,
        # The SAME client instance, deliberately: a resumed run reaches the
        # same nodes, and two clients would mean two gRPC channels and two
        # independently-cached tokens for one worker process.
        dialogue=dialogue_client,
        ask_client=ask_client,
        subject_filter=ExecutionConsumer.RESUME_SUBJECT_FILTER,
        durable_name=ExecutionConsumer.RESUME_DURABLE_NAME,

    resume_task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.create_task(

    )

    # vertical's work-queue stream.

        publisher=publisher,

    queue_result_task: asyncio.Task[None] = asyncio.create_task(
        queue_result_consumer.run(), name="queue-result-consumer"
    )

    # JetStream stream, and the two subjects this feature needs only reach

        queue_park_reaper.run(), name="queue-park-reaper"

        # Integration-test mode: one idle cycle, then exit.
        _request_shutdown()

    exit_code = 0
    stop_task = asyncio.create_task(_stop_event.wait(), name="stop-waiter")
    try:
        done, _pending = await asyncio.wait(
            {
                stop_task,
                consumer_task,
                resume_task,
                trigger_scheduler_task,
                chain_trigger_task,
                queue_result_task,
                reaper_task,
            },
            return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
        )

            if task is not stop_task and not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is not None:
                # A dead consumer (e.g. ConsumerConfigMismatchError on a stale
                # durable) is FATAL: exit nonzero so an on-failure restart

                # failure — a clean exit 0 here would mean no restart and a
                # green status for a worker that consumes nothing (triage #14).
                # ANY of the three dying is fatal — a live run-job consumer
                # with a dead resume or queue-result consumer would accept work
                # and then never wake anything it parked.
                _log.error("consumer exited", task=task.get_name(), err=str(task.exception()))

        _log.info("workflow-svc-worker shutdown begin")
        await consumer.close()
        await resume_consumer.close()
        await trigger_scheduler.close()
        await chain_trigger.close()
        await queue_result_consumer.close()
        await queue_park_reaper.close()
        # Closed once, not once per consumer — both share the instance.
        await dialogue_client.close()
        consumer_task.cancel()
        resume_task.cancel()
        trigger_scheduler_task.cancel()
        chain_trigger_task.cancel()
        queue_result_task.cancel()
        reaper_task.cancel()
        if not stop_task.done():
            stop_task.cancel()
        # Every task this worker started, or shutdown silently leaves one
        # running.
        await asyncio.gather(
            consumer_task,
            resume_task,
            trigger_scheduler_task,
            chain_trigger_task,
            queue_result_task,
            reaper_task,
            stop_task,
            return_exceptions=True,
        )
        await ask_client.close()
        await publisher.close()
        await pool.close()

        healthz_server.shutdown()
        healthz_server.server_close()

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Process entrypoint. Returns the desired exit code."""
    configure_logger(level="INFO")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="workflow_svc.worker",
        description="workflow-svc-worker: JetStream consumer host (ExecutionConsumer)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--once",
        action="store_true",
        help="run one idle cycle and exit (integration-test mode)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cfg = cfg_mod.load()
    except cfg_mod.ConfigError as exc:
        structlog.stdlib.get_logger("workflow_svc.worker").error("config load failed", err=str(exc))
        return 1
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_serve(cfg, once=args.once))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0

    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

If you want to:

- **Regenerate proto stubs (Go/Python/TS)**: `make proto`
- **Regenerate only TS proto stubs**: `make proto-ts`
- **Lint proto**: `make proto-lint`
- **Check proto breaking changes**: `make proto-breaking`
- **Run Go tests for a service**: `cd services/<svc> && go test -short ./...` (or `make <svc>-test`)
- **Run one Go test by name**: `go test -run '^TestName$' ./internal/...`
- **Run Go integration tests**: `go test -tags=integration -run '^TestName$' ./tests/integration/...` (or `make <svc>-test-int`, Docker required)
- **Run all Go modules + coverage file**: `make go-test` (or `make go-test-short` to skip testcontainers)
- **Check Go coverage gate**: `make go-coverage`
- **Tidy Go modules**: `make go-tidy`
- **Vet Go code**: `go vet ./...` (from service dir)
- **Run Vitest for one workspace**: `pnpm test`
- **Watch Vitest (TDD loop)**: `pnpm test:watch`
- **Run one Vitest test by name**: `pnpm test -- --run -t "<name>"`
- **Run Vitest with coverage**: `pnpm test -- --coverage`
- **Recompile Paraglide i18n messages**: `pnpm --filter @omnicore-platform/platform-chrome run compile-messages` (then hand-wire `frontends/platform-chrome/src/paraglide/messages.ts`)
- **Audit i18n locale parity/ICU/glossary**: `npx tsx scripts/i18n-audit.ts`
- **Fast glossary-only i18n check**: `cd frontends/platform-chrome && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/glossary.regression.test.ts`
- **Regenerate Range location-wizard geo shards (offline)**: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts` (network refresh: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts --fetch` first, to repopulate `scripts/geo-sources/`)
- **Lint an MFE**: `pnpm lint`
- **Typecheck an MFE**: `pnpm typecheck`
- **Bring up the whole stack (baked images)**: `make up` (`SCOPE=<vertical>` to limit, `CLEAN=1` to wipe volumes, `BUILD=1` to rebuild images from fresh proto)
- **`make up` never builds two MFE images at once — not even the ones `BUILD=` did not name**: each Vite build takes an 8GB Node heap, so the guarded loop (`_build-guarded`) builds non-MFE images in parallel and MFE images strictly one at a time. That guard used to cover only the `BUILD=`-selected set, while `up`'s final `docker compose up -d` carried no `--no-build` and every locally-built service keeps its `build:` context — so anything `BUILD=` missed and `stack-pin-images.py` could not snapshot (which is *everything* on a machine with no bare `:dev` tags left to snapshot from) was built by **compose** instead, all at once. 11 concurrent Vite builds either die with `ResourceExhausted: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build" ... cannot allocate memory` or drives an OOM-kill spiral that wedges the Docker daemon, so `make up` just *hangs* with no error at all. `up` now plans the absent set itself (`platform/scripts/plan-implicit-builds.py`), builds it through the same guard, and passes `--no-build` so any remaining hole fails loudly instead of fanning out. `make dev` deliberately keeps compose's implicit build: its MFE layer is host-side vite servers, not containers, so only service images can be built there. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_build_guarded.py platform/scripts/test_plan_implicit_builds.py -q`.
- **AI backend mode (unified across verticals, `omnicore_svc_runtime.ai`)**: real inference-server litellm/vLLM (over Tailscale) is now the default for `make up`/`make dev` — `AI_DEV_MODE` is unset/false in `.env.example`. `AI_TEST_MODE=true` → StubLLM (deterministic, wins over `AI_DEV_MODE`). `AI_DEV_MODE=true` → local Ollama backend (`platform/compose/ollama.yml`, litellm alias `ollama-dev`). Old per-service flags (`STUDIO_AI_DEV_MODE`, `RANGE_AI_DEV_MODE`, `DIALOGUE_AI_DRAFT_DEV_MODE`) are gone — hard cutover. Per-vertical model pins (`RANGE_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `qwen3.5:9b`; `STUDIO_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss:20b`; `LITELLM_DRAFT_MODEL` for dialogue, default `gpt-oss:20b`) live as env-overridable defaults in `range-svc.yml`/`range-svc-worker.yml`/`studio-svc.yml`/`studio-svc-worker.yml`/`dialogue-svc.yml`/`dialogue-svc-worker.yml`.
- **Boot-time AI reachability probe + offline/force-live escape hatches**: `make up`/`make dev` run a preflight (`platform/scripts/ai-live-probe.py`) before compose starts, checking each in-scope AI-capable vertical's resolved model against the real gateway. Reachable → live mode, printed per-vertical. Unreachable with local Ollama available → loud degraded-fallback banner, never a silent per-call swap. Unreachable with no Ollama → the target fails outright. `OFFLINE=1` (formerly `RANGE_AI_MODE`, now `AI_OFFLINE_MODE`, vertical-scope-agnostic) skips the probe entirely and forces local Ollama — airplane-mode / no-Tailscale case. `REQUIRE_LIVE=1` turns an unreachable gateway into a hard failure instead of a degraded fallback. `STUB=1` means `AI_TEST_MODE=true` (deterministic StubLLM) — it does NOT mean local Ollama; use `OFFLINE=1` for that.
- **Hot-reload dev stack (services + MFEs)**: `make dev` (`SCOPE=` honored)
- **Boot an isolated walled local stack (own compose project, own hostname, one published port)**: `make up STACK=<name>` — needs `*.localhost` to resolve, which works out of the box on macOS (no other OS supported yet). Not seeded automatically: a fresh stack has no users until you also run `make seed STACK=<name>`.
- **Hot-reload a walled local stack**: `make dev STACK=<name>` — the walled overlay is derived from `dev`'s OWN compose file set (never `up`'s), so a scoped `dev` never references a service (e.g. an MFE container) that `dev` itself doesn't bring up, and shell-bff's dev-mode volumes (the `/workspace` bind + Go module/build caches) survive the per-stack mtls rewrite instead of being silently dropped.
- **A bare `make up` in a worktree warns before driving the SHARED stack**: `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME ?= omnicore-platform` is identical in every worktree and is only reassigned inside the `STACK=` block, so `make up` / `dev` / `seed` / `down` / `clean` / `cypress-run` with no `STACK=` drives that ONE project and its volumes from whatever worktree you happen to be in. `up`/`dev`/`seed`/`down`/`clean`/`cypress-*` now print the derived `STACK=<name>` you probably wanted and pause 3s. It is warn-only, never fatal — silence it with `OMNICORE_NO_STACK_WARN=1` (or pass `STACK=platform` to say you meant the shared one). Silent in the primary checkout, which legitimately owns that project.
- **List running local stacks and their URLs**: `make stacks` — the state column is `up` / `down` / `orphaned` / `orphaned-up`. `orphaned` means the worktree that owned the pin no longer exists on disk; `orphaned-up` means that AND it is still live and serving, so its port must not be reused.
- **Drop pins whose worktree is gone**: `make stack-gc` (`DRY=1` to preview). Nothing used to remove a pin except an explicit `release` run from the owning worktree, so a `git worktree remove` left its entry behind forever, holding a name and a port. `gc` deliberately refuses to drop an `orphaned-up` pin — that stack is still serving, and freeing its port would let a second stack claim it.
- **Retire a stack for good**: `make stack-release STACK=<name>` — drops the registry pin, this worktree's generated `.omnicore/` files for it, AND its per-stack image tags. Prefer this over `stack.py release` now that image tags are per-stack, since the bare script cannot clean those up (it owns identity only, no docker).
- **Print one stack's URL**: `make stack-url STACK=<name>`
- **Seed a walled stack's default data**: `make seed STACK=<name>` (same idempotent seed as the primary — 1 org + 1 workspace + 10 role-combo users + 1 range exercise; `make seed` with no `STACK=` seeds the primary)
- **Open psql against a walled stack's postgres**: `make psql STACK=<name>`
- **Publish a walled stack's postgres+nats on two extra host ports for GUI DB clients**: `DB_PORTS=1` (only meaningful with `STACK=<name>`, e.g. `make up STACK=review DB_PORTS=1`)
- **Hot-reload one MFE into a walled stack**: `make <vertical>-mfe-dev-federated STACK=<name>` — routes `/<vertical>-mfe/` through that stack's own ingress to your local vite server instead of the baked image. Safe to run for several MFEs at once in the same stack: each invocation re-reads every OTHER live `--hot` MFE's probed port from `.omnicore/hot-<stack>-*.port` and re-adds it, so starting a second one doesn't 502 the first; the port file is removed automatically when that MFE's dev server exits.
- **Run the cross-stack isolation gate (12 vectors)**: `make stack-isolation-test STACK_A=<name> STACK_B=<name>` (both stacks already up; the unwalled primary's name here is `platform`, e.g. `STACK_A=platform`)
- **Reach a walled stack's admin consoles**: same single published port, different sub-hostnames — `auth.<name>.localhost:<port>` (Keycloak), `grafana.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `minio.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `prom.<name>.localhost:<port>`
- **Reach a walled stack's Vault**: no ingress route and no host port, deliberately — `docker exec` into the stack's vault container (see `make vault-pki-bootstrap`)
- **Provision mTLS PKI for a walled stack**: `make vault-pki-bootstrap STACK=<name>` — writes issued certs to that stack's own `.omnicore/secrets-<name>/mtls` tree (`CA_OUT_DIR`) instead of the shared `platform/secrets/mtls` the unwalled path uses.
- **Force a stack's pinned port to re-probe**: `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py resolve --stack <name> --reprobe` — only needed when something else grabbed the previously-pinned port while the stack was down; a plain `make up STACK=<name>` never re-probes an already-pinned, currently-live port out from under itself.
- **Where stack names/ports are pinned**: `~/.omnicore/stacks.json`, machine-wide (NOT per-worktree) — a stack name becomes a hostname and a compose project, both of which are machine-global, so one registry arbitrates them across every worktree. The unwalled `platform` stack is SKIPPED there, since it legitimately owns the bare `:dev` tags.

## CI runs on the promotion to `develop`, not on the PR

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,
the promotion of `main`: Go `-race` + coverage gate, frontend unit + coverage,
Python *integration* (testcontainers), migration lint, i18n, pact, proto
compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on
`ubuntu-24-arm-2core` and the `changes` job scopes both matrices to the services
a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

The cheap class still runs on the PR, again on the merge commit to `main`, and
again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a
GitHub-hosted ARM64 larger runner: billed, but at the ARM rate, out of its own
concurrency pool rather than the plan's 60 standard slots, and seconds-to-a-few-
minutes per job. So `main` keeps per-merge signal for these:

| Check | Workflow | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lint, Compose config validation, Keycloak realm-export lint, Branch-protection doc sync, Load-harness lib tests | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Secret Scan (gitleaks) | `secret-scan.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Action Lint | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Go Vuln Scan (govulncheck) | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| golangci-lint (new-issues-only) | `go-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, **PR only** |
| py lint / lint + typecheck + unit (`<svc>`), lint + typecheck (shared python libs) | `python-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (scoped to changed services; `integration (<svc>)` stays develop-only) |
| No duplicate Prometheus metrics in a boot graph | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image | `sign-and-verify.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (that workflow has no `main` trigger) |
| go test -short (every changed module) | `go-test.yml` | self-hosted, **push to `main` only** |

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

Consequences worth internalizing:

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

## Testing policy — Cypress e2e

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch. Any PR that adds or changes a user-facing surface owes a spec under `frontends/cypress/cypress/e2e/<vertical>/`, landed in the same branch — as does any change to login, session, invite, or org-role gating, UI diff or not. Backend-only PRs (proto, migration, service handler, BFF route with no UI consumer) don't.

Ownership is split by file, not by team:

- **Feature dev owns:** the spec files themselves, and `support/selectors.ts`.
- **QA/QC-stewarded:** the shared foundation — `cypress.config.ts`, `support/{e2e,commands,personas}.ts`, `tasks/**`, `fixtures/personas.json`.

Two things that bite:

- A spec absent from a workflow's `--spec` list did not run. Wiring it into the relevant GitHub workflow is part of authoring the spec — check that the workflow actually seeds the state the spec needs.
- `e2e.yml` is non-required and posts no check, so a green PR is not evidence a spec ran. Verify locally against `make up`.

# Frontend design system guardrails

- Per `tdd-react` on `tailwind.preset.ts` as the source of truth for `cog-*`: an
  undefined token emits no CSS and is silently invisible, not an error. This branch
  found 52 phantom tokens across 233 occurrences, including 3 passing tests that
  asserted classes rendering nothing. Grep the preset before using any `cog-*` class
  — a test asserting an undefined class is not a safety net.
- **Never inline raw hex or arbitrary Tailwind values** (`text-[#fff]`,
  `border-[1.5px]`) at a call site — define a token in the preset instead.
- **Bare numeric spacing/size utilities are banned** (`p-4`, `gap-6`, `min-h-11`) in
  favor of named `cog-*` rungs. For hit targets specifically, use `min-h-tap` /
  `min-w-tap` (44px) — never `min-h-11`.
- **WCAG 2.5.8 hit areas:** don't enlarge the visible box to hit 44×44. Move the
  drawn box into an inner `aria-hidden` span at its original size, and put the tap
  rungs on the interactive element wrapping it. Applied 7x this branch — follow the
  established pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- **Any new axis added to `tailwind.preset.ts`'s `theme.extend` must be registered in
  `frontends/ui/src/lib/cn.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge` config.** An unregistered axis
  makes `tailwind-merge` silently DELETE one of two conflicting classes — 5 live
  defects found this branch from exactly this (`text-heading-md`, `bg-cog-ai`,
  `shadow-cog-e1`, `border-field`, letterSpacing). The `CN_axis_parity` rule in
  `platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs` gates it.
- **`Design parity` (`platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs --ci`) is PR-blocking.**
  Its counts are ratchets — they may only go down, never up. A matcher change
  requires re-running with `--update` in the same PR, so the rule diff and the count
  diff review together.
- Test process for any change here: see the `tdd-react` skill.

The generated artifacts (ingress config, walled overlay, per-stack secrets, hot-port files) stay in each worktree's own `.omnicore/`, since they are built from that worktree's source.
- **A stack name belongs to the worktree that created it**: reusing the same `STACK=<name>` from a different worktree is refused, not silently shared — `stack 'x' is owned by a different worktree -- refusing to touch it.` naming both paths. Without this, two worktrees would resolve the same compose project and the second `make up` would recreate the first's containers from its own source, i.e. a reviewer's stack silently serving another branch's code. Pick a different name (`make up STACK=<name>-2`) or release it with `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py release <name>`.

The GPU can't be meaningfully partitioned, so a real shared instance is future work; until then, budget ~792 MiB/stack for it specifically, on top of the capacity figures below.
- **Local stack capacity**: one walled stack is ~76 containers behind one published port, ~50-80s to boot. Four stacks running concurrently (305 containers) measured 8.23 GiB of a 23.43 GiB Docker Desktop VM (35%) once idle — idle stacks compress well below their boot-time peak, so the ~4.2 GiB/stack figure in the design spec (measured immediately post-boot) overstates steady state.
- **EVERY locally-built image is tagged per stack, not just shell-mfe**: a walled stack runs `omnicore-platform/<svc>:<tag>-<name>` (e.g. `range-svc:dev-review`, and `:dev-hotreload-review` under `make dev`); shell-mfe keeps its own `:walled-<name>`. Before this, the compose project, hostname, port, mTLS tree and litellm keys were all per-stack but the ~67 `image: ...:dev` tags were machine-global, so ANY worktree's `make up STACK=<x> BUILD=...` replaced the image a different, still-running stack would resolve on its next container recreate — that stack then silently served another branch's code, and all 11 isolation vectors still passed because every one of them tested *runtime* isolation. `up`/`dev` now snapshot the tags via `docker tag` (metadata only, no rebuild) just before `up -d`; see `platform/scripts/stack-pin-images.py`.
- **A pinned stack does NOT pick up a newer `:dev` on restart — that's the point**: the snapshot is sticky, so a plain `make up STACK=<name>` keeps serving the image IDs it was pinned to even after another worktree rebuilds `:dev`. To deliberately adopt the current build, pass `REPIN=1` (`make up STACK=<name> REPIN=1`). A `BUILD=` run always builds straight into the per-stack tag, so it needs no `REPIN`.
- **Vector 12 is image provenance**: it fails a stack whose containers sit on a machine-global (unsuffixed) tag, and separately flags a container whose running image ID no longer matches what its own tag resolves to — i.e. the tag was rebuilt underneath a live container. The unwalled `platform` stack is SKIPPED there, since it legitimately owns the bare `:dev` tags.

- **Run the k6 load-test harness**: `make load-test` (`SUITE=<name>`, default `smoke`; requires a running stack)
